summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's central nervous system lymphoma, was admitted for his 14th cycle of maintenance chemotherapy with intravenous rituximab and high-dose methotrexate. He reported stable symptoms, including persistent floaters, and denied new neurological or systemic complaints. He received rituximab followed by high-dose methotrexate with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization. Leucovorin rescue was initiated once his methotrexate level dropped to 0.31 µM and was continued until levels fell below 0.06 µM. His kidney function remained stable throughout, and liver enzymes showed mild, non-progressive elevation. An MRI of the brain with contrast revealed no new enhancing lesions or significant changes, indicating no lymphoma progression. He tolerated the regimen well without complications and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue his home medications and monitor for any concerning symptoms, with follow-up scheduled in four months.
